Year 1 STEAM unit · Questions About My World

Wonderful and Weird Things in Our World

Seven lessons of big questions for Year 1. Each week we look closely, ask why, and find out how the world works.

???

About this unit

This is our Year 1 STEAM unit, Questions About My World. Each week starts with a big question. We look, test, draw and talk. In lesson 5 we ask how machines know what to do. Lessons 6 and 7 then take our first steps into algorithms with block code and simple sequences.

    What we will learn

    Week 1

    Weird and wonderful animals

    We are learning to sort animals by their body parts and say why they have them.

    • Body parts help animals stay alive.
    • We can sort animals in different ways.
    Week 2

    Why are trees so important?

    We are learning to say why trees matter and what they give us.

    • Trees make fresh air and give animals homes.
    • Roots hold the soil.
    Week 3

    Will it float?

    We are learning to guess, test and sort things that float and sink.

    • A prediction is a guess before we test.
    • Testing shows if we were right.
    Week 4

    How do planes fly?

    We are learning to test paper planes and find the best design.

    • A fair test keeps things the same.
    • We record and compare results.
    Week 5

    How do machines know what to do?

    We are learning to give and follow clear steps, like making a sandwich or a cake.

    • People give machines instructions.
    • Steps in the wrong order mean disaster!
    Week 6

    Our first block code

    We are learning to take a first step into algorithms with block code.

    • Blocks are instructions we snap together.
    • A set of steps in order is an algorithm.
    Week 7

    Simple sequences

    We are learning to put simple steps in order and see how a sequence makes an algorithm.

    • A sequence is steps in the right order.
    • A clear sequence makes an algorithm.

    Big words

    adaptation
    A special part of an animal's body that helps it stay alive.
    habitat
    The place where an animal lives.
    camouflage
    Colours and patterns that help an animal hide.

    Ask at home

    Which strange animal did you like best? What part of its body helps it, and why? Can you think of an animal near us with a body part that helps it?

    What we do this week

    1. Look closely at strange animals and say what we notice.
    2. Work out why each body part helps, using habitat and food.
    3. Move animals to the habitat where they belong and explain why.
    4. Draw, label and colour our own animal on the iPads.

    Big words

    oxygen
    The part of the air we need to breathe.
    roots
    The parts of a tree under the ground. They hold the soil.
    forest
    A big place full of trees.

    Ask at home

    Can you find three things at home that are made from trees? Look for paper, wood and cardboard.

    Week 5

    How do robots know what to do?

    A robot only does what people tell it. It follows every step exactly, in order. Can you give the robot the right steps?

    Make it with the robot

    Choose what to make. Tap the steps in the right order. Then run the robot.

    Steps. Tap to add.

    The robot's list

      Big words

      instruction
      A step that tells someone or something what to do.
      order
      Which step comes first, next and last.
      algorithm
      A set of clear steps in the right order.

      Ask at home

      Tell a grown up the steps to make toast or to brush your teeth. What would go wrong if you did the steps in the wrong order?
